newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt could top London as finance centre - survey.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt could top London as finance centre - survey.

text.p: Frankfurt could overtake London as Europe's key financial centre if Britain opts out of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), according to a survey of 500 European directors published on Wednesday.
It is the first time since property consultants Healey and Baker began their survey in 1990 that European businessmen had thought Frankfurt could be in a position to take London on.
When asked which city would be Europe's top financial centre over the next five years if Britain did not participate in EMU, three times as many directors named Frankfurt.
But if Britain did participate in European Monetary Union, then 61 percent put London top of the list.
"Politicians, bankers and businessmen have been engaged in heated debate over the EMU issue," said Healey and Baker partner Paul Orchard-Lisle.

"Now, for the first time, the survey provides hard evidence that non-participation could hand over economic advantage to Frankfurt. The City (of London) employs 750,000 people and contributes 39 percent of London's GDP. Can we afford to put this at risk?" he added.
